To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
transient brain ischemia and followed reperfusion induce enhanced formation of FYN-PSD95- NR2A complex, which is mediated by activation of NMDARs and L-VGCCs.

transient brain ischemia and reperfusion induced formation of a ternar complex of Fyn, NR1A and NR2A, and that the formation was attenuated by NMDA receptors antagonist or L-type voltage gated calcium channels antagonist.

transient brain ischemia induces formation of a ternaray complex: Fyn, PSD95 and NR2A and the association increases after reperfusion, and the increase is attenuated by inhibiting NMDA receptor and L-VGCC activation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms underlying ischemic neuronal cell damage.
the molecular mechanism of brain ischemia induced enhancement of NMDAR function, which may provide new therapeutic strategies for ischemic stroke.
the mechanism of NMDA-induced excitotoxicity in brain ischemia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the activation of NMDAR and L-type voltage gated Ca2+ channel facilitates formation of a Fyn-PS95-NMDAR2A complex, which results in potentiation of the NMDAR function and contributes to ischemic cell death.
activation of L-VGCC facilitates the formation of the Fyn-PSDs-95-NR2B complex, which may contribute to ischemic cell death.
the formation of Fyn-PSDs95-NR2 complex is a novel mechanism underlying ischemic neuronal injury.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the activation of NMDARs and L-VGCCs after ischemic injury leads to the formation of a ternay complex of Fyn–NR2A–PSD95, which may contribute to the potentiation of NMRARs function and ischemic neuronal cell injury.

the activation of NMDARs and L-VGCC during brain ischemia followed reperfusion facilitates formation of a complex: Fyn-NR2A-PSD95, which may contribute to potentiation of NMRAs and contribute to neuronal death.

activation of NMDAR and L-VGCC mediates the formation of a ternay complex: Fyn-NR2A-PSD95, which may contribute to potentiation of NMRAR function and neuronal cell death after transient brain ischemic injury.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NMDA receptors are activated during transient ischemia and the activation is mediated by L-type voltage-gate Ca2+ channel.
activation of NMDARs and L-VGCC during brain ischemia and early reperfusion may contribute to the formation of Fyn-NR2A complex and Fyn-PSR95-NR2 complex.

activation of NMDARs and L-type VGCC during ischemia and reperfusion facilitates formation of Fyn-PS95-NR2B complex in hippocampus, which may contribute to NMDAR potentiation and neuronal cell death after ischemia.
